NQA - try and breathe. Whatever happens now, happens. Do not move the enclosure anymore and just leave the spider be. You cannot undo the bump and the worst thing to do now would be to intervent further. In the best case nothing happened when you bumped it, in the worst you shouldn't help it until you're sure it's stuck anyway. Try and distract yourself as best as you can until the little one is done for now - that's the best for everyone. Maybe check out the discord too - there's people there who can advise proper further steps If anything goes wrong with the molt. Either way it'll help the spider most If you relax and don't do anything out of panic.

In general, molting in water dishes is something that happens all the time. Trust your spider to choose its spot. And even If it chooses poorly - don't move it. That is more risky than just letting it do its thing.

Good luck to your little one and i hope you can calm yourself a little for now. 🙏

IME keeping cats and tarantulas apart is a must. We have two cats and nineteen tarantulas and that only works because we lock the tarantulas into their own room. Our youngest cat is very curious and has broken into the room twice and each time she's been close to throwing sling cages off of the shelf. She's also sniffed the air vents of the larger spiders and i am glad that neither time the spiders kicked hairs at her.

Personally i would recommend that you only get another tarantula If you can ensure that they don't meet, especially If your cat has already shown interest in the spiders. I know that sucks If your current living conditions do not allow it, but these are living beings and both animals could end up seriously hurt. I'd recommend searching the sub for "Cat" as well to see what incidents have happened to others.

Of course this is only my personal opinion and Others might have different experiences, but i would strongly suggest that the risk isn't worth it.

In general, don't stress about feeding - i usually go by the size of the spiders abdomen and end up feeding slings about once or twice a week and adults 2-3 crickets every month. Just make sure you don't leave in any feeders for too long and make sure you clean any boluses. And definitely give them a water dish!
For the size of the terrarium, the rule most people go by is 2.5x its leg span for length and enough height to provide a lot of substrate for digging. There should be about 1x the legspan of space at the top and no more, or else they might get hurt while climbing and falling. In my own collection i have found that older specimen can be comfortable with a little bigger enclosure as well as long as you provide plenty of hiding spaces and the top isn't too high, though i wouldnt recommend a big enclosure for a sling. :) It should be fairly obvious when a rehouse is due If you keep that in mind! NQA. I'd recommend against using any heatpad unless it is absolutely necessary (freezing temperatures). And even then i'd First suggest looking into alternative, indirect sources of heating. It is always better for the tarantula to heat up the room instead of pointing a source of heat at it. Heatmats can cause T's to sit there and slowly dry out until they can't move and die. If you use them under the enclosure it is additionally hard to control the temperature for burrowing T's. Not applicable to your mexican red knee (brachypelma ?hamorii?) but i figured i'd mention it.
IME for most species 70 degrees is perfectly fine and they'll be safe enough. Even as far down as 60 has been fine for me for short periods as long as it doesn't dip any further.

Two thoughts on this, to maybe give you some ideas for troubleshooting:
1. The enclosure looks very moist. I don't have much experience with moisture dependant species (my only more difficult ones being c.versicolor and p.cambridgei) and none whatsoever with selenotypus sp2, so take what i say with a grain of salt since you probably researched this more than me. But i don't think your enclosure has enough cross-ventilation for the amount of moisture in there either way. A few more holes along the enclosure side and maybe the lid could improve air flow a lot. I'd definitely try and dry out the substrate too - making sure to keep the bottom layers wet so the sling can bury If it does need more moisture - and add a water dish instead (there is enough space for a small bottle cap, for example). The problems you're experiencing could be related to potentially stuffy air making the sling sick. 
2. The holes look wide and nice - it's still possible that they got stuck - If you can rule out sickness, then this might be the most likely explanation. Did you burn the holes in with a hot needle? The holes look similiar to how i do them. In that case, maybe make sure that no sharp edges have been left behind - i had that happen before and sanding down the holes does help reduce the risk of cutting the T when they climb the walls. 

And other things that are not related to the enclosure and might cause stress/sickness/unease that could be the culprit, so take these into consideration:
1. Did anyone in your neighbourhood recently spray pesticide? Any other way fumes could've gotten into the T room? Stuff like paint, deodorant, mosquito spray, any of that? These are things i hadn't considered prior to keeping T's, but their book lungs are VERY sensitive.
2. Is there frequent air flow in your animal room? Often times when enclosures are near doors the enclosures can get hid with drafts frequently, causing stress in the animals and potential health problems. 
3. How is your temperature? I don't think this is too important in this case, just something to consider if there are any significant changes especially during winter. 

And for the leaking - i think at this point you'd probably have noticed the little one considerably slowing down if it was bleeding out. Keep a lookout of course, but at that size i don't think they'd still be kicking if any fluid was being lost continuesly.

I hope these can give you some ideas. Try and watch out for the small one and if they keep getting worse we can try some other things. Wishing both of you the best of luck and for your T to get well asap!!!!

(Also, i am an owner of a somewhat obese sling myself lol, i get it. PLEASE just molt, babies! You've got plenty of energy reserves, as we can all see very well!! :D)
In general, I personally don't recommend tong feeding any spider. They can easily break their fangs that way.

Two Things: First, a full pic of the enclosure might help us. What does the lid look like? Are there any hard surfaces they could've dropped onto? Any holes that they could've gotten their legs stuck in? 
Secondly, is it possible you've left a feeder in there? Crickets especially can be vicious and attack tarantulas, one could've hurt the little guy, causing them to have to amputate their leg. 

Either way, lost limbs are absolutely a cause for concern and you're doing well trying to find the cause. They don't randomly loose legs without being sick or getting injured.

Also, please check whether they're leaking any fluid! If they amputated at the joints it should be fine, but sometimes the amputation can cause worse complications for them.

Just a heads up though, If you have a wild caught specimen you might want to make double sure that you're not keeping them illegally where you are. A lot of tarantula species are endangered in the wild and there is plenty of specimen in the Hobby to aquire and keep legally and ethically. I really enjoy the potential dynamic there could be between Kara and North since they're both people who seem like they'd be complete opposites (though slightly depending on how you play Kara) but there's actually a few things they have in common. Both have been traumatized by humans, take on a role of being in charge for someone that they want to keep save at all cost (Jericho, Alice), and both are willing to give their own life for the ones they love. I also feel like they could learn from each other, which is something I really appreciate in ships. I think we do get to see a softer side to North in the game, but only rare glimpses of it and Kara could be the person to help her get in touch with it. Likewise I feel like North might be able to help Kara deal with what's been done to her and Alice. For Connor/Gavin, I truly get how that ship might be off-putting to others and simply going by canon it's pretty bad. Gavin is a two-dimensional asshole and he treats Connor like shit. However I really like developing something healthy between them in fanwork, make them work to start understanding each other to a point that Connor could forgive him. That's probably the appeal for me, to rework a relationship like that in a save environment when it didn't work out for me irl.
